headline: High-risk filesystem overlap and output-chaining: Mentat can write shared files while pdf.js can consume PDFs, creating medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat writes to the filesystem and shares state via filesystem with other instances; pdf.js reads PDF files and runs in a browser-based worker model. If Mentat places attacker-controlled content into files that pdf.js later opens, the pathway exists in default workflows. The interaction is documented only at profile level, so uncertainty stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Mentat writes untrusted content into a PDF or adjacent file that pdf.js opens
IF pdf.js is used on files produced by Mentat without content provenance checks
mitigations: Open only files from trusted directories
Add a manual review step before pdf.js opens Mentat-produced files
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
Rename or quarantine generated files before viewing
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between file producers and consumers

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat reads and writes selected files and has broad network egress; pdf.js processes PDF documents from files. If the same workspace contains sensitive PDFs or source files, Mentat can expose contents through its model-provider calls while pdf.js can surface those documents locally. The shared filesystem path makes leakage plausible in default setups, but not inevitable.
conditions: IF sensitive PDFs or source files are stored in a shared workspace
IF Mentat sends file contents from that workspace to its model provider
mitigations: Separate sensitive PDFs from coding workspaces
Disable or restrict Mentat access to confidential directories
Review which files Mentat is allowed to open
Use redacted copies for pdf.js review
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs or per-agent mounts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, and its concurrency model shares state with other instances via filesystem. pdf.js also reads files, so both can touch the same workspace. Concurrent edits or file rewrites can corrupt git state or overwrite artifacts; the shared mutable surface is dangerous by default and can cause irreversible loss.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same checkout or directory
IF pdf.js writes or rewrites files that Mentat is also editing
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files
Commit or stash changes before switching agents
Use read-only mounts for pdf.js
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared workspaces

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals and pdf.js can render or process documents, so a workflow can chain Mentat output into pdf.js inputs or vice versa. If pdf.js treats generated files as authoritative, errors can propagate without verification. The pair does not prove automatic action-taking, so medium is the higher justified level.
conditions: IF pdf.js consumes files generated by Mentat without human verification
IF Mentat-derived text or markup is treated as authoritative input by downstream processing
mitigations: Require human review before downstream use
Compare generated files against source originals
Mark Mentat outputs as drafts
Keep pdf.js outputs separate from action-triggering workflows
requires-engineering: add validation gates before any automated follow-on step

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles do not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Mentat handles model-provider API keys and source code, while pdf.js touches PDFs, but no regulated-data flow or jurisdiction conflict is documented. The other agent is not cited beyond confirming no mismatch evidence.
conditions: IF regulated PDFs or secrets are introduced into the shared workflow
IF an external deployment policy imposes residency or retention constraints not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated documents out of the pair
Review retention settings for the model provider
Use separate storage for secrets and PDFs
Document data-handling policy for both tools
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
